testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use:
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems. These have two separate braking systems that share one set of controls. Each system operates the brakes on different axles.

questions.question: If you do not drain the air brake tanks, what can happen?

options.text: Water freezing and causing brake failure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water freezing and causing brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks must be drained to remove water and compressor oil. If you do not drain them, water can build up inside. In cold weather, this water can freeze and cause your brakes to fail.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a front brake limiting valve, where should you set the control?

options.text: Set the control to the off position.
Keep the control at the halfway mark.

questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. You should always leave it set to "normal" to get full stopping power.

questions.question: When driving downhill, you should brake until you reach a speed that is ____ below your safe speed, then release the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When driving downhill, brake until your vehicle reaches a speed 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake pedal. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Emergency brakes in air brake systems must use mechanical force. Air pressure can leak away over time, so it cannot be relied on to keep the brakes engaged.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle should not lose more than 6 psi of air pressure in one minute during a leakage test. Know the safe leakage rate for your vehicle.

questions.question: While driving, what keeps spring brakes in place?
questions.explanation: Air pressure holds spring brakes in place while you drive. If air pressure drops too low, the springs will automatically activate the brakes.

questions.question: How do you remove water and compressor oil from an air storage tank?

options.text: The water and oil are siphoned out of the tank.
A drain valve is opened to remove the water and oil from the tank.
The water and oil are removed automatically as the brakes are used.
A sponge is used to soak up the water and oil.

questions.correctAnswerText: A drain valve is opened to remove the water and oil from the tank.
questions.explanation: Open the drain valve at the bottom of air storage tanks to remove water and compressor oil. These must be removed daily from manually operated tanks. If left to build up, they can damage your brakes.

questions.question: How often should you drain air tanks with manually operated drains?
questions.explanation: Drain air brake tanks with manual drains at the end of each driving day. This removes water and oil that can damage your brakes.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, how fast do air brakes work?

options.text: Only if the green lever on the control panel is pushed down.

questions.explanation: Air brakes have a delay of about half a second or more after you press the brake pedal. Air must travel through the lines to reach the brakes. This is different from hydraulic brakes in cars, which work right away.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: Hold enough air for only one braking cycle.
Hold enough air so the brakes work several times if the compressor stops.
Hold air only during an emergency.
Hold enough air for more than 1,000 braking cycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air so the brakes work several times if the compressor stops.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: What can happen if you use the parking brake in wet, freezing weather?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may suddenly release by themselves.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: In wet, freezing weather, the parking brakes may freeze. This can prevent the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual brake system, what should you do?

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up so fuel reaches the engine.
Wait for air pressure to build in both systems.
Start driving right after the engine starts.
Pump the pedal about 20 times, then start driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for air pressure to build in both systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving, let the compressor build air pressure to at least 100 psi in both brake systems.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air leaves the storage tanks.
The temperature of air entering the storage tanks.
The temperature of air leaving the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: Emergency brakes are required on:
questions.explanation: All trucks, tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how long should it take for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi?
questions.explanation: Air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems in about 45 seconds.

questions.question: What color light warns you when the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working?
questions.explanation: The ABS warning light is usually yellow. If the light comes on, the ABS is not working, but you still have regular brakes.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how are the air tanks set up?

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You choose which system to use.
Only one side of the vehicle has working brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. Each system has its own air tanks and is connected to a single set of brake controls.

questions.question: Emergency brakes are required on:
questions.explanation: All trucks, tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes held by mechanical force.

questions.question: When do spring brakes turn on?

options.text: When air pressure gets too low.
When you press a dashboard control.
When tires have low tread depth.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure gets too low.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes turn on automatically when air pressure drops to an unsafe level. When you see the low pressure warning, safely exit the road and stop while you can still control the brakes.

questions.question: Why do some air brake systems use alcohol?

options.text: To prevent ice from forming in air brake valves.
To help the compressor work more efficiently.
To lubricate parts of the braking system.
To prevent rust from forming on air brake valves.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent ice from forming in air brake valves.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. This device adds alcohol to the braking system to stop ice from forming.

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: To stop normally in a vehicle with air brakes, push down the brake pedal. The harder you push the pedal, the more air pressure is released to the brakes.

questions.question: When should you not use the parking brake?

options.text: When your vehicle is stopped on a level surface.
When your vehicle is stopped on a slight incline.
When your vehicle's brakes are very hot.
When your vehicle's other braking systems are working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: When your vehicle's brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if the brakes are very hot from going down a steep hill or if the brakes are wet and it is freezing. Using the parking brake on hot brakes can damage them. Using brakes when they are wet in freezing weather can cause them to freeze, making the vehicle unable to move.

questions.question: When should you test the low pressure warning signal?
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work properly. After the system fills with air, test it by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air from the system. The warning light should come on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: What is true about vehicles with dual air brake systems?

options.text: They keep full air pressure in the brakes even when the engine is off.
They keep some air pressure in the brakes when the engine is off.
The engine must run to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work.
They do not need time to build air pressure before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine must run to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, you must let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi of pressure in both the primary and secondary brake systems.
